header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Using individual neurons as these units has had some success (Olah et al., 2020; Bills et al., 2023), but a key challenge has been that neurons are almost always polysemantic, with nearly every neuron activating for several unrelated types of feature (Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.quote: Neural networks often contain “polysemantic neurons” that respond to multiple unrelated inputs.
polysemantic neurons are a major challenge for the circuits agenda
the process of detecting cars and dogs was deeply intertwined in the model

args.text:
Verdict: not supported

The sentence makes two claims about Olah et al. (2020), *Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits*. The first, that polysemanticity is a key challenge, is supported. The second, that neurons are "almost always" polysemantic, with "nearly every neuron" responding to several unrelated feature types, is not.

What the source supports: the article says "polysemantic neurons are a major challenge for the circuits agenda, significantly limiting our ability to reason about neural networks" (distill:zoom-in/r1/b65).

What the source does not say: its only general statement is that "Neural networks often contain “polysemantic neurons” that respond to multiple unrelated inputs." (distill:zoom-in/r1/b62). "Often" is a much weaker claim than "almost always", and the article gives no per-neuron rate or statement that nearly every neuron is polysemantic. Its concrete example is a single neuron, InceptionV1's 4e:55, which "responds to cat faces, fronts of cars, and cat legs" (distill:zoom-in/r1/b63).

Bills et al. (2023) does not appear in the library as its own document. It is cited only in the reference list of the sparse autoencoder paper (arxiv:2309.08600/v3/p10), so I could not check what it says about individual neurons. The sentence's claim that neurons have had "some success" as units rests on that citation, which I could not verify.

Suggested fix: replace "almost always polysemantic, with nearly every neuron..." with "often polysemantic, responding to multiple unrelated inputs (Olah et al., 2020)".
